topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Overview of Cancer Hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's learning outcomes, connects them to previous lectures on tumorigenesis, and presents the foundational framework of the hallmarks of cancer.

topics.label: Deregulation of Growth Signaling Pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations in cell-surface receptors and downstream signaling cascades enable self-sufficiency in growth signals and resistance to inhibitory signals.

topics.label: Differentiation Block in Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how malignancies prevent precursor cells from exiting the cell cycle and completing terminal lineage differentiation in blood and intestinal tissues.

topics.label: Resistance to Apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the mitochondrial apoptotic pathway and the alterations in p53 and Bcl-2 family regulators that permit cancer cells to evade programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative Immortality, Cellular Senescence, and Intrinsic Hallmark Summary
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail telomere dynamics, mechanisms of overcoming senescence to achieve immortalization, and conclude the review of cell-intrinsic growth-control hallmarks.

topics.label: Metabolic Reprogramming in Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the Warburg effect, systematic metabolic rewiring across tumor types, and the generation of oncometabolites that reinforce tumorigenesis via epigenetic alterations.

topics.label: Tumor Angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses the requirement of blood vessel recruitment for sustaining tumor growth and the balance of molecular signals regulating the angiogenic switch.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Genetics of Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the multi-step invasion-metastasis cascade, the seed-and-soil paradigm, and the genomic characteristics associated with metastatic clones.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Summary
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session by summarizing how individual hallmarks integrate in cancer progression, recommending literature, and transitioning to questions.
